sanskrit_verse:
भर्तुर्द्रोहे यथा नार्याः पुंसः पुत्रसुहृद्वधे ।
दोषो भवेत् तथा न्यासे भक्षितोपेक्षिते नृणाम् ॥
transliteration: bhartur drohe yathā nāryāḥ puṃsaḥ putra-suhṛd-vadhe | doṣo bhavet tathā nyāse bhakṣita-upekṣite nṛṇām ||
sph_interpretive_translation: As a woman’s betrayal of her husband equals the killing of his son or friend, similarly, when men neglect or abandon those under their protection after consuming them, it constitutes a comparable offense.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority arises through capacity to sustain and protect.
Causation is established by consumptive dependence and subsequent abandonment.
Capacity-based responsibility demands proportional response to relational neglect.
Restoration logic requires reversal of harm caused by breach of protective duty.
Consciousness alignment necessitates recognition of interdependence as sacred trust.
executable_legal_axioms: IF an individual consumes resources or labor of another AND fails to provide reciprocal sustenance THEN liability for restorative completion is triggered.
IF a person holds guardianship or custodial authority AND abandons that role AFTER deriving benefit THEN automated restoration protocol initiates.
IF dependency has been created through consumption OR integration THEN withdrawal without restoration invokes dharmic realignment process.
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that failure to fulfill custodial or protective duties—especially after exploiting the dependent party—is legally equivalent to gross dereliction of dharma. The threshold of responsibility is determined not by formal position alone, but by the causal relationship of consumption and reliance.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality identifies the act of consuming another's energy or resources as foundational to establishing relational obligation. Anupūrvaśaḥ reveals that neglect follows exploitation in sequence, making the exploiter responsible for completion. Proportional responsibility aligns with the degree of dependency induced. Non-punitive reality rule ensures correction occurs through restoration, not suffering.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Completion Process wherein all consumed value is returned or compensated through service.
Assign Responsibility Assumption Protocol requiring the violator to restore integrity within the affected community.
Implement Capacity Restoration Mechanism ensuring future ability to uphold protective roles before resuming authority.
Enact Integrity Reintegration Sequence wherein the offender undergoes conscious recalibration to prevent recurrence.
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of Law. Dharma is hereby restored. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness stands as the supreme adjudicator.
